items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast independent, similar-sized haploid and diploid generations with unequal land-plant generations, using an isomorphic cycle with documented demographic turnover and life-cycle plasticity.

can_transfer.text: Life-cycle structure in Ulva thalli, with species and specimens unspecified: independent, macroscopic, nearly indistinguishable haploid and diploid generations (Wichard et al. 2015; Bessho 2024).
can_transfer.support: Free-living, macroscopic, nearly indistinguishable from the diploid generation: isomorphic haplodiplontic alternation (Wichard et al. 2015; Bessho 2024).

can_transfer.text: Generation time in U. mutabilis, with specimens and site unspecified: 3 to 5 weeks; retain only for the algal comparator (Wichard et al. 2015).
can_transfer.support: generation time of *U. mutabilis* is 3 to 5 weeks (Wichard et al. 2015).

can_transfer.text: Phase turnover in the natural U. pertusa population in the Seto Inland Sea: dominance alternated after 11 to 20 months, with sex ratio near 1:1 (Hiraoka and Yoshida 2010).
can_transfer.support: phase dominance alternated after 11 to 20 months with no seasonal pattern, and the sex ratio stayed near 1:1 (Hiraoka and Yoshida 2010).

can_transfer.text: Drying response in Ulva sp., with specimens and site unspecified: linear electron flow stops, cyclic PSI flow persists and recovers faster than PSII after rewetting (Gao et al. 2011).
can_transfer.support: in desiccated *Ulva* sp. linear electron flow stops and PSI-driven cyclic flow persists and recovers faster than PSII on rewetting (Gao et al. 2011).

cannot_transfer.text: Phase-demography coefficients from Hughes and Otto (1999) cannot become measured Ulva parameters: their model was parameterised on Gracilaria.
cannot_transfer.support: parameterised on the red alga *Gracilaria*, not *Ulva*

cannot_transfer.text: Embryophyte matrotrophy, embryo retention and protective spore-wall constraints cannot be parameterised from this marine cycle; the card describes no maternal provisioning, retained zygote, sporopollenin wall or cuticle.
cannot_transfer.support: no zygote retention or maternal provisioning described, a free-living diploid thallus, no sporopollenin spore wall, no cuticle.

cannot_transfer.text: Early land-plant demographic rates cannot be set to Ulva rates; the card expressly excludes that transfer between independently evolved cycles.
cannot_transfer.support: Do not use *Ulva* rates for early land plants.

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast tall, leafless trees supported by a broad primary body and shallow roots with woody, deeply rooted architectures, using the reconstructed Wattieza–Eospermatopteris whole plant.

can_transfer.text: Minimum reconstructed stature for the South Mountain Wattieza–Eospermatopteris whole plant, species unspecified: at least 8 m, reconstructed from a 6 m trunk section and crown (Stein et al. 2007; Berry 2019).
can_transfer.support: 'At least 8 m', a tree-fern-like reconstruction from a 6 m trunk section and a crown (Stein et al. 2007, abstract).

can_transfer.text: Shallow rooting geometry in New York Eospermatopteris bases attributed to Wattieza: roots 0.7-1 cm wide, radiating 1-2 m and penetrating to 30 cm (Stein et al. 2020).
can_transfer.support: Adventitious roots on the trunk base, 0.7-1 cm wide, rarely branched, radiating 1-2 m and penetrating to 30 cm; probably replaced as the tree grew (Stein et al. 2020).

can_transfer.text: Conducting-strand presence in Gilboa Eospermatopteris casts: coalified cauline xylem occurs with little cellular anatomy; encode strand presence without hydraulic coefficients (Xu et al. 2017).
can_transfer.support: Gilboa casts preserve coalified, 'clearly formerly woody' cauline xylem strands with little cellular anatomy (Xu et al. 2017)

can_transfer.text: Architecture of the reconstructed Gilboa Wattieza–Eospermatopteris tree: an unbranched trunk bears digitate, three-dimensional lateral branch systems in longitudinal ranks; modular shedding is the reported architectural interpretation (Stein et al. 2007).
can_transfer.support: Unbranched trunk with large lateral branch systems in longitudinal ranks, shed as frond-like modules; branches are digitate and three-dimensional

cannot_transfer.text: The 85% cell-wall fraction in Xinicaulis wood cannot set Wattieza support costs or hydraulic properties: it belongs to another cladoxylopsid.
cannot_transfer.support: Cell walls fill 85% of Xinicaulis wood

cannot_transfer.text: A numerical growth or gap-colonisation rate cannot be derived from the description of Eospermatopteris as weedy and relatively fast-growing; Stein et al. (2020) offer an inference.
cannot_transfer.support: Stein et al. (2020) call the tree 'weedy', relatively fast-growing and able to colonise gaps (inference).

cannot_transfer.text: A maximum height of about 10 m cannot be used as a verified measurement; it comes from an unchecked press report.
cannot_transfer.support: A press report of the 2012 paper gives 'up to about 10 m' (not checked).

cannot_transfer.text: Spore characters and reproductive output cannot be parameterised: even the statement that reproduction used spores is attributed to a press summary rather than verified reproductive material.
cannot_transfer.support: Not verified in the sources read; reproduction was by spores, not seeds, per a press summary.

borrowed.support: tracheid wall type is unknown and the cellular detail comes from the related Xinicaulis.

items.doubts: The conducting-tissue entry combines Gilboa xylem evidence with cellular detail from Xinicaulis; only the latter is borrowed. Eospermatopteris is explicitly treated as part of the reconstructed whole plant. Wattieza's primary versus secondary growth mode remains unsettled.

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast trilete-spore plants with permanent-cryptospore eophytes and their different conducting tissues, using charcoalified fragments that directly associate anatomy with in situ spores.

can_transfer.text: Annularly thickened tracheids in charcoalified Cooksonia pertoni from the Welsh Borderland assemblages can define a conducting-tissue morphotype (Edwards & Kenrick 2015).
can_transfer.support: tracheids with annular thickenings in charcoalified C. pertoni (Edwards & Kenrick 2015)

can_transfer.text: Permanent dyads or tetrads in eophytes, including Partitatheca from North Brown Clee Hill, provide alternative cryptospore states rather than trilete-spore states (Edwards et al. 2014).
can_transfer.support: permanent dyads or tetrads in eophytes (Edwards et al. 2014).

can_transfer.text: Preserved lengths of Cooksonia, species not separated, in Lang's Downtonian compressions from England and Wales: about 1-6 cm; use as fragment lengths (Edwards & Kenrick 2015).
can_transfer.support: Lang's Cooksonia compressions are about 1-6 cm long (Edwards & Kenrick 2015).

cannot_transfer.text: Tracheids cannot be assigned to eophytes from the assemblage-wide front-matter state; their reported conducting cells are leptoid-like food conductors (Edwards et al. 2021a).
cannot_transfer.support: leptoid-like food-conducting cells only in eophytes (Edwards et al. 2021a).

cannot_transfer.text: Gametophyte–sporophyte dependence cannot be established from North Brown Clee Hill transfer-cell thalli: their gametophyte identity is hypothesised and no sporophyte is matched (Edwards et al. 2021b).
cannot_transfer.support: Thalloid fossils with transfer cells from North Brown Clee Hill are a hypothesised eophyte gametophyte, not attributed to a sporophyte (Edwards et al. 2021b).

cannot_transfer.text: Population abundance and relative taxon frequencies cannot be inferred from these transported, selectively preserved fragments; the card recommends presence data.
cannot_transfer.support: use as presence data with large unobserved-habitat uncertainty, not as abundance data.

cannot_transfer.text: Global lineage-origination dates cannot be assigned from regional first appearances; major innovations may have occurred elsewhere (Edwards & Richardson 2004).
cannot_transfer.support: first appearances here are minimum-age constraints for the region, not for the clade.

items.doubts: The basal charcoal horizon has unresolved upper Ludlow versus basal Pridoli assignments. Front-matter height summarises preserved Cooksonia lengths, not complete plants; conducting tissue and spore states combine distinct member lineages.

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast preserved fungal–cyanobacterial association with assumed mutualistic nutrition and early lichen cover, because Rhynie material records spatial association without establishing nutrient-exchange rates.

can_transfer.text: Spatial association in Rhynie W. reticulata thin sections: Taylor et al. (1997) report three-dimensional nets enclosing sheathed coccoid cyanobacteria; use as their anatomical interpretation.
can_transfer.support: Hyphae extend into the base of each depression and form a three-dimensional net; each net space encloses a coccoid cyanobacterium with a thick sheath.

can_transfer.text: Reproductive structures in Rhynie W. reticulata material were reported as endospores and soredia (Taylor et al. 1997); encode that interpretation without specifying production or dispersal rates.
can_transfer.support: Reproduction was by endospores and soredia.

cannot_transfer.text: Stable mutualistic carbon-for-nutrients exchange cannot be assigned to W. reticulata from morphology; Berbee et al. (2020) explicitly reject that inference.
cannot_transfer.support: Berbee et al. (2020) say a stable, mutualistic fungus-photobiont relationship cannot be inferred from the morphology.

cannot_transfer.text: Nitrogen-fixation capacity or rate cannot be treated as observed in W. reticulata; the proposed contribution of its filamentous partner is an inference.
cannot_transfer.support: Karatygin et al. suggest the filamentous partner could add nitrogen fixation, which is an inference.

cannot_transfer.text: Weathering rates cannot be taken from Porada et al. (2016) as measurements of W. reticulata: their Late Ordovician non-vascular vegetation flux is a simulation output.
cannot_transfer.support: this is a model output to test, not data.

cannot_transfer.text: The first compelling lichen occurrence cannot be assigned to Winfrenatia; Berbee et al. (2020) instead identify Lochkovian charcoalified thalli.
cannot_transfer.support: They regard the Lochkovian charcoalified thalli as the earliest compelling lichens.

items.doubts: The original hyphal interpretation is disputed by an abstract-only reinterpretation as cyanobacterial sheaths. No dimensions or exchange rates are supplied. The Pragian range is narrower than the Pragian-to-possibly-earliest-Emsian dating note.

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast small belowground allocation and lateral fertile architecture in Lochkovian South China with coeval terminal-sporangium floras, using one rooted whole specimen within a provincial assemblage.

can_transfer.text: Preserved aerial stature in the single uprooted Zosterophyllum shengfengense specimen from the Xitun Formation near Qujing: 98 mm (Hao et al. 2010).
can_transfer.support: Aerial axes 98 mm tall in the one uprooted whole specimen of Zosterophyllum shengfengense (Hao et al. 2010).

can_transfer.text: Belowground allocation in that Xitun Z. shengfengense specimen: root-like axes about 20 mm long, root:shoot 0.028 and about 3% of biomass; retain as a specimen-specific estimate (Hao et al. 2010).
can_transfer.support: rhizome with root-like axes about 20 mm long; root:shoot 0.028, root-like axes about 3% of biomass

can_transfer.text: Fertile architecture in Xitun Formation Xitunia spinitheca: helically arranged stalked sporangia with unequal valves and distal spines on the larger abaxial valve (Xue 2009, 2012).
can_transfer.support: *Xitunia spinitheca*: stalked sporangia in a helical arrangement, flattened, two unequal valves, the larger abaxial valve with long spiny appendages at its distal margin.

cannot_transfer.text: Hydraulic efficiency and root uptake coefficients cannot be extracted from Z. shengfengense: efficient water use and strong uptake are alternative ecological interpretations, not measured rates (Hao et al. 2010).
cannot_transfer.support: with efficient water use or strong uptake by the root-like axes (Hao et al. 2010).

cannot_transfer.text: Flora-wide or Lochkovian-wide root:shoot allocation cannot be fixed at 0.028; the estimate rests on one Z. shengfengense specimen rather than the other assemblage members.
cannot_transfer.support: A model with a single parameter for this stage rests on one specimen.

cannot_transfer.text: Spore identity and matching to dispersed assemblages cannot be transferred: Xitun has no reported in situ spores linking its plants to Posongchong or Xujiachong.
cannot_transfer.support: With no in situ spores, the flora cannot be tied to the Posongchong and Xujiachong spore records (F4).

cannot_transfer.text: An exact 413 Ma fossil age cannot be used; the card recommends stage-level timing because late Lochkovian fish biostratigraphy narrows the unit only qualitatively.
cannot_transfer.support: use stage-level timing; the 'late Lochkovian' fish age narrows it only qualitatively.

items.doubts: Front matter records compression preservation, but the text says this is assumed. The taxon count, specimen counts and locality totals are incomplete; published geographic province labels also differ.

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast multiplication of terminal sporangia on sparsely branched axes with simpler fertile units, using a sizeable preserved shoot whose supposed synangia proved preservation artefacts.

can_transfer.text: Minimum preserved extent and fertile-unit count in Y. oblonga NMV P236587, Eglinton Cutting: at least 280 mm and almost 20 terminal fructifications (McSweeney et al. 2021).
can_transfer.support: Y. oblonga specimen NMV P236587 (Eglinton Cutting) is at least 280 mm tall with almost 20 terminal fructifications on naked axes (McSweeney et al. 2021).

can_transfer.text: Axis width in Victorian Y. oblonga material: 1.0-4.2 mm; retain this species-specific range (McSweeney et al. 2021, Table 2, as reproduced in McSweeney 2024).
can_transfer.support: Y. oblonga 1.0-4.2 mm

can_transfer.text: Fertile-unit architecture in Victorian Y. oblonga fragments: 1-6 sporangia per fructification, each 2.7-7.0 mm long; use as an architectural multiplier without spore counts (McSweeney et al. 2021).
can_transfer.support: 1-6 sporangia per fructification, each 2.7-7.0 mm long (McSweeney et al. 2021).

cannot_transfer.text: Synangial fusion cannot be coded from the type material; the apparent synangium is a preservation artefact rather than demonstrated fertile anatomy.
cannot_transfer.support: 'synangium' should not be coded from the type material.

cannot_transfer.text: Tracheid anatomy or hydraulic conductance cannot be inferred from the central line in Frenchmans Spur specimen NMV P256741; no tracheids have been observed.
cannot_transfer.support: A 0.2 mm central line, read as a vascular trace, is visible in one Frenchmans Spur axis (NMV P256741), but no tracheids have been seen.

cannot_transfer.text: A decumbent rooting architecture or clonal-spread mechanism cannot be assigned from NMV P236587: apparent horizontal-to-upright axes are equivocal in transported material.
cannot_transfer.support: possibly a decumbent habit, but McSweeney et al. (2021) call this equivocal because the specimen is allochthonous.

cannot_transfer.text: Spore output cannot be calculated as an observed quantity from fructification counts; the proposed tens of sporangia are arithmetic, and no spore numbers exist.
cannot_transfer.support: no spore numbers exist

items.doubts: The Lochkovian first-stage entry is explicitly conservative rather than demonstrated. Silurian Yea dates and the South African identification remain disputed. The principal redescription was read through its reproduction in McSweeney (2024).

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast size-dependent reproductive allocation across a heterogeneous lycophyte stem grade, using member-specific dimensions and a fossil record that constrains its radiation and decline.

can_transfer.text: Axis width in Bathurstia, with species and measured specimens unspecified: 4-12 mm; use as this member's size range rather than a grade-wide diameter (Huang et al. 2025).
can_transfer.support: the zosterophyllopsid Bathurstia has axes 4-12 mm wide

can_transfer.text: Belowground allocation in the single whole-plant Zosterophyllum shengfengense specimen, locality unspecified here: root-like axes about 20 mm long and root:shoot 0.028 (Hao et al. 2010).
can_transfer.support: Zosterophyllum shengfengense (about 20 mm long, root:shoot 0.028; Hao et al. 2010)

can_transfer.text: Sporangial-volume scaling in the zosterophyllopsid sample of Huang et al. (2025): per-spike volume 1-864 mm3 increases with axis width, conditional on assumed 0.6 mm thickness; individual measurement taxa and sites are unspecified here.
can_transfer.support: Sporangial volume per spike runs 1-864 mm3 across zosterophyllopsids and scales with axis width (Huang et al. 2025, assuming 0.6 mm sporangial thickness).

can_transfer.text: Minimum fossil occurrence at late Ludlow Bathurst Island: ten fertile plants of seven taxa, mostly zosterophylls; retain as a record constraint rather than an origination date (Kotyk et al. 2002).
can_transfer.support: The oldest assemblage is late Ludlow, Bathurst Island, with ten fertile plants of seven taxa (Kotyk et al. 2002).

cannot_transfer.text: Measured lifespan, generation time or demographic r/K parameters cannot be assigned from differences in spike volume; the life-history interpretation is inferential (Huang et al. 2025).
cannot_transfer.support: an inference from sporangial volume, not measured lifespan.

cannot_transfer.text: Uniform G-type tracheid anatomy and hydraulic parameters cannot be assigned across the grade; anatomy remains unknown for most species.
cannot_transfer.support: anatomy is unknown for most species (Huang et al. 2025; Claisse et al. 2025).

cannot_transfer.text: Universal homospory cannot be imposed on the inclusive grade: nested barinophytes include heterosporous plants, despite the front-matter heterospory state.
cannot_transfer.support: The barinophytes, nested in the grade, include some of the oldest heterosporous plants (Capel et al. 2022, citing Bonacorsi et al. 2020, 2021).

cannot_transfer.text: A maximum whole-plant height of 44 cm cannot be transferred from Z. confertum; that value describes preserved axes and may underestimate complete stature.
cannot_transfer.support: preserved axes reach 44 cm in Z. confertum, so true heights of large species were probably greater

items.doubts: The last-stage field says Frasnian, while its note says Last = Givetian. Height combines near-complete plants with preserved axis lengths. Heterospory is coded absent despite heterosporous members in the inclusive grade; the Pridoli gap also remains unresolved.

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast size and reproductive allocation among coeval leafless species, using divergent spike volumes while retaining species-specific conducting and rhizomatous architectures.

can_transfer.text: Belowground allocation in the single uprooted Z. shengfengense whole plant from the Xitun Formation, Yunnan: root:shoot 0.028 and root-like axes about 3% of biomass (Hao et al. 2010).
can_transfer.support: Root:shoot ratio is 0.028, with root-like axes about 3% of biomass (Hao et al. 2010)

can_transfer.text: Conducting architecture in Z. myretonianum from the Scottish Carmyllie Beds: a single median tracheid strand; encode anatomy without assigning hydraulic rates (Lang 1927).
can_transfer.support: Z. myretonianum has a single median strand of tracheids (Lang 1927)

can_transfer.text: Near-complete stature in Z. baoyangense from Duyun, Guizhou: 45.4 mm; retain as this species' preserved size rather than a genus-wide height (Huang et al. 2025).

can_transfer.support: small Z. baoyangense (4.3-16.8 mm³)

can_transfer.text: Estimated per-spike sporangial volume in coeval Z. australianum from the Pragian Duyun bed: 133.8-211.1 mm³ under assumed 0.6 mm sporangial thickness; keep separate from Z. baoyangense (Huang et al. 2025).
can_transfer.support: Z. australianum (133.8-211.1 mm³)

cannot_transfer.text: Genus-wide rooting architecture, biomass allocation or clonal-spread rate cannot be fixed from Z. shengfengense; the complete rooting system represents one species and one specimen.
cannot_transfer.support: This is observed for one species; extending it to the genus is an inference.

cannot_transfer.text: Measured lifespan and spore output cannot be assigned to Z. baoyangense or Z. australianum from their estimated sporangial volumes; both quantities remain inferred.
cannot_transfer.support: The pair gives a measured contrast in body size, inferred lifespan and spore output.

cannot_transfer.support: Preserved axes of Z. confertum reach 440 mm, so true heights of larger species were probably greater.

items.doubts: The Pridoli gap conflicts with reported Z. qujingense occurrences. Conducting anatomy, complete rooting architecture and reproductive-volume estimates come from different species; they must remain separate rather than forming a synthetic genus-wide plant.

items.chosen_to_contrast: Contrast a durable single-celled diploid stage with a multicellular sporophyte, using haplontic relatives that also demonstrate vegetative drought tolerance and specialised zygospore biology.

can_transfer.text: Haplontic baseline for Zygnematophyceae, presented as a class-level synthesis without specified specimens: the diploid phase is a durable single cell followed by meiosis (Kenrick 2018).
can_transfer.support: the diploid phase is a durable single cell

can_transfer.text: Culture-age dependence in Z. circumcarinatum, site unspecified: desiccation tolerance increases with age, while drying induces ROS scavenging, chaperones and aquaporins (Rippin et al. 2017).
can_transfer.support: In *Z. circumcarinatum*, tolerance rose with culture age, and drying induced ROS scavenging, chaperones and aquaporins (Rippin et al. 2017).

can_transfer.text: Desiccation response in Zygnema cultures, species and culture provenance unspecified: old cultures survived at 84% relative humidity; only slowly acclimated cells survived rapid drying at 10% (Holzinger and Pichrtová 2016, as summarised).
can_transfer.support: old cultures survived desiccation at 84% relative humidity, and only slowly acclimated cells survived rapid drying at 10%

can_transfer.text: Meiosis in Closterium ehrenbergii zygospores, species named in the reference but specimens and site unspecified: meiosis begins during greening and two non-sister nuclei abort; retain as species-specific biology (Kasai and Ichimura 1983).
can_transfer.support: In the desmid *Closterium*, meiosis begins in the greening zygospore and two non-sister nuclei abort (Kasai and Ichimura 1983)

cannot_transfer.text: Ancestral land-plant body simplicity cannot be reconstructed directly from living Zygnematophyceae; their simple morphology may be secondary rather than ancestral.

cannot_transfer.support: the sources read describe no provisioning of the zygote by a parent thallus.
